title: Change the label roll that is nearly used up for the full spare
instruction: One of the label printers is about to run out of labels. Fit the spare roll to it and put the old roll in the grey bin.
context: Done by: shipping and receiving clerks and packers (O*NET 43-5071, 53-7064). A label printer that runs out mid-batch stops the packing line, so the operator changes the low roll first. Nothing names the low roll; the cue is how much label is left and its red end-of-roll stripe. Unlike TK-JJD7XA and TK-2GRHHM (battery swaps where the depleted unit is named or tiled), the robot must find which of three machines needs the change, and the spare's core must fit over a spindle.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Three label printers (fixed, dark grey painted housings, the same): a body 100 mm front to back, 100 mm wide and 40 mm tall, centred 34 cm in front of the arm bases, at 13 cm left of the midline, on it, and 13 cm right. Each has a black label-exit slot 64 mm wide and 6 mm tall (25 to 31 mm up) on the face toward the robot, and at its deck's centre a black steel spindle 30 mm across and 22 mm tall topped by a 22 mm lead-in 6 mm tall (28 mm above the deck in all). Label rolls (loose, rigid, 40 mm tall, standing on end over a spindle or on the table): white labels wound on a brown cardboard core, with a 36 mm hole through the core. A full roll is 86 mm across with a 46 mm core (170 g). The nearly used-up roll is 50 mm across with a 48 mm core: a thin band of labels whose top 12 mm is red, the end-of-roll stripe (40 g). Each printer has a roll on its spindle; one is the nearly used-up roll, the other two are full. A full spare roll stands on the table and a grey plastic bin (loose but heavy, 1.5 kg; 108 x 108 mm outside, 100 x 100 mm inside, 4 mm walls and floor, 40 mm tall) stands on the table, each centred 17 cm in front of the arm bases in line with one of the printers. Lot A: the nearly used-up roll on the left printer, the spare in front of the left printer, the bin in front of the centre printer. Lot B: the nearly used-up roll on the centre printer, the spare in front of the left printer, the bin in front of the right printer. Lot C: the nearly used-up roll on the right printer, the spare in front of the centre printer, the bin in front of the right printer. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial. Score 0, judged over the whole trial from the video, if either full roll on a printer ever moves more than 10 mm from where it started (lifted off, even if put back). Otherwise, at the end, with no gripper within 5 mm of the spare or the old roll and everything still: score 1.0 when the spare is on the spindle of the printer that held the nearly used-up roll (its bottom within 1 mm of the deck, its axis within 4 mm of the spindle's and within 5 degrees of vertical), the two full rolls are still on their own spindles the same way, and the old roll is in the bin (its centre inside the bin's walls, its lowest point within 20 mm of the bin floor, any orientation). Score 0.5 when all of that holds except that the old roll is anywhere on the table (its lowest point within 2 mm of the table top, any orientation) instead of in the bin. Score 0 otherwise: the spare on the wrong printer, resting on a spindle top or the old roll, in the bin or on the table; the old roll still on its spindle, on a printer, on a rim or off the table; a roll held or moving. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Put a roll over each printer's spindle (the nearly used-up roll on the lot's printer: A left, B centre, C right) and stand the spare and the bin on the table in front of the lot's printers (A: spare left, bin centre; B: spare left, bin right; C: spare centre, bin right). Nothing is consumed (the binned roll is reused). Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: A bench mock-up. A real desktop label printer holds its roll on a spindle under a lid and feeds the web through a print head; here the roll drops over an open spindle with no lid or label web. The rolls are rigid; the kit has only solid cylinders, so each ring is drawn as overlapping upright cylinders, its edge scalloped by about 2 mm. The bin is loose only so the lots can move it. Masses and friction (1.2) are simulator values.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
